case_name: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab and Another

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Jacob Mathew ... Appellant
versus
State of Punjab and Another ... Respondents
Coram: R.C. Lahoti, C.J., G.P. Mathur, P.K. Balasubramanyan, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 05 August 2005

LAHOTI, C.J.:
1. This appeal deals with the legal standard of criminal negligence required to prosecute a medical practitioner under Section 304A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for causing death by negligence.

2. Gross Negligence Requirement: A simple lack of care, an error of judgment or an accident is not sufficient to constitute criminal negligence under Section 304A. In civil law, negligence is actionable on preponderance of probabilities; in criminal law, the negligence must be gross, reckless and amounting to a culpable disregard for human life and safety (mens rea of reckless disregard).

3. Safeguards for Medical Practitioners: To protect medical professionals from malicious or frivolous criminal prosecution, the Supreme Court laid down mandatory guidelines: (1) A private complaint shall not be entertained unless supported by a credible medical expert opinion; (2) An investigating officer shall not arrest a doctor unless gross negligence is established by independent medical testimony.
